title: Every colour represented at each vertex in a bipartite graph
statement: Let $G$ be a finite bipartite simple graph with minimum degree $\delta > 0$. Then there is an edge colouring $C$ of $G$ using $\delta$ colours — that is, a function assigning to each edge one of the colours $1, 2, \ldots, \delta$, not required to be proper — such that every colour is represented at every vertex: for each vertex $v$ and each colour $i$, some edge incident with $v$ is assigned colour $i$.
replaced:
Ex 6.1.6 (Gupta)

6.1.6 Show that if $G$ is bipartite with $\delta > 0$, then $G$ has a $\delta$-edge
colouring such that all $\delta$ colours are represented at each vertex. (R. P. Gupta)
